Question: Describe your support for Anthropic's Model Context Protocol: agent-to-tool communication, tool discovery, MCP-exposed APIs and data sources.
Response: MCP is the primary integration pattern in our architecture. GHCP SDK natively supports MCP — agentic loops discover and invoke MCP tools as their primary mechanism for interacting with enterprise systems. All enterprise integrations are exposed as MCP servers: Workday, Greenhouse, LinkedIn, ServiceNow, Microsoft Graph, Dataverse, ACS, HeyGen. MCP servers are governed through APIM AI Gateway which provides: auth injection (the agent developer never manages tokens), rate limiting, content safety filtering, and discovery (agents discover available MCP tools through APIM's tool catalog). APIM also provides a REST-to-MCP gateway — auto-generates MCP tool definitions from OpenAPI specs, making any REST API MCP-compatible. MCP servers support both HTTP and Streamable HTTP transports. Tool discovery is centralised through APIM's managed catalog with metadata (description, auth requirements, rate limits, SLA, owning team).
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK native MCP, APIM AI Gateway (MCP governance), REST-to-MCP gateway, MCP server catalog
POC Demo: POC1: Show MCP tool discovery from APIM catalog. Demonstrate Maconomy REST API auto-bridged to MCP via APIM gateway.

Question: Describe your A2A implementation: AgentCards, task lifecycle, streaming, push notifications. Are agents both A2A clients and servers?
Response: A2A is supported via APIM AI Gateway for cross-platform agent collaboration. AgentCards: each Hosted Agent publishes an AgentCard via APIM describing capabilities, supported tasks, and interaction protocols. APIM registers and serves AgentCards. Task lifecycle: JSON-RPC based task creation, status updates, and completion. Long-running tasks supported with SSE streaming for real-time status. Push notifications via webhooks for task state changes. Agents are both A2A clients (can discover and invoke external agents via AgentCards) and servers (expose capabilities for external agents to invoke). APIM governs all A2A interactions: authentication (Entra-based), policy enforcement, rate limiting, and audit logging. This enables WPP agents to collaborate with agents on different stacks — WPP Open, partner agencies, external platforms.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (A2A governance), AgentCards, JSON-RPC, SSE, Entra authentication
POC Demo: POC2: A2A demonstration — external candidate agent discovers WPP's Interview Coordinator via AgentCard, negotiates interview times via JSON-RPC task lifecycle.

Question: Can agents collaborate with agents on entirely different stacks (e.g., Palantir, Salesforce)? Describe security, auditability, and policy governance for federation.
Response: Yes. A2A protocol provides the interoperability layer. Any platform that implements A2A (Google, Salesforce, and growing ecosystem) can collaborate with WPP's agents. APIM AI Gateway provides the federation governance layer: (1) Security — Entra-based authentication for all federated A2A calls. Mutual TLS for transport security. APIM policies enforce allowed external agents and operations. (2) Auditability — all federated interactions logged in APIM with full request/response capture. OTEL traces span across federated calls. Audit logs flow to Log Analytics with 7-12 year retention. (3) Policy governance — APIM policies control which external agents can interact, what operations are permitted, token limits, rate limits, and content safety filtering on federated traffic. Data residency policies apply to federated calls — PII from a German workflow cannot be sent to non-EU endpoints even via A2A.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (federation governance), A2A protocol, Entra authentication, OTEL cross-boundary tracing

Question: Does the platform support emerging protocols (UCP, AG-UI, AP2) or provide extension points for new protocols without platform upgrades?
Response: APIM AI Gateway provides protocol extensibility without platform upgrades. APIM supports custom policies that can mediate any HTTP-based protocol — new protocols (UCP, AG-UI, AP2) can be supported by adding APIM policy definitions and MCP server wrappers. The MCP layer provides a consistent tool interface: any new protocol can be wrapped as an MCP server, making it immediately available to agentic loops without changes to the core runtime. AG-UI support is planned for Foundry in H2 2026. For emerging protocols: the architecture is designed for protocol evolution — add a new APIM policy and/or MCP server, register in the tool catalog, and agentic loops can consume the new protocol immediately. No platform upgrade required.
Key Technologies: APIM custom policies, MCP server wrappers, protocol-agnostic architecture
